questions.q: What is the minimum horizontal distance of court and yards (setback)?
questions.n: The code explicitly requires a minimum of 2 meters for the horizontal distance of courts and yards to ensure proper light and ventilation.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of toilet facilities for Group A Dwellings?
questions.n: Each dwelling unit under Group A must have at least one sanitary facility to be considered habitable.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness of Foundation Footings on Dwellings units?
questions.n: The National Building Code sets 250mm as the minimum thickness to ensure structural stability for Group A dwellings.

questions.q: What is the minimum depth below the ground of Foundation Footings on Dwellings units?
questions.n: A minimum depth of 600mm is required to ensure the foundation is properly seated below the natural grade.

questions.q: What is the minimum Floor Live Load at Ground Floor Level?
questions.n: The ground floor must be able to support a minimum live load of 200 kg/sqm due to higher expected activity and storage.

questions.q: What is the minimum Floor Live Load at succeeding Upper Floors?
questions.n: Upper floors have a slightly lower minimum live load requirement of 150 kg/sqm compared to the ground floor.

questions.q: What is the minimum Wind Load Capacity for Roof?
questions.n: The code requires the roof structure to withstand at least 120 kg/sqm of wind pressure.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of every Stairs in Group A Dwellings?
questions.n: 750mm is the absolute minimum width allowed for stairs within an individual dwelling unit.

questions.q: What is the minimum Rise and Run for Steps of every Stairs?
questions.n: The code allows a maximum rise and minimum run of 200mm each for stairs in Group A dwellings.

questions.q: What are the required Open Spaces left after deducting the Outermost Face of the Bldg.?
questions.n: The term 'Yard' refers to the required open space that must be left on a lot between the building and the property lines.

questions.q: What is the minimum front setback for R1 residentials?
questions.n: For R-1 residential zones, the code mandates a 4.5m front setback and 2.0m on the sides.

questions.q: Which section of the NBCP governs the Building Height Limits (BHL)?
questions.n: This heading refers to the regulatory constraints on how tall a building can be based on zoning.

questions.q: What are the Building Height Limits for Residential R-1 & Townhouses R4?
questions.n: R-1 and R-4 developments are limited to 3 storeys or a height of 10 meters.

questions.q: What are the Building Height Limits for Condominiums R-5?
questions.n: R-5 is high-density residential, allowing for significant height up to 18 storeys or 54 meters.

questions.q: What are the Building Height Limits for Residential Basic R-2 & R-3?
questions.n: Basic R-2 and R-3 zones are limited to the same 3 storey/10m height as R-1.

questions.q: What is the Building Height Limit for Residential Maximum R-2?
questions.n: Maximum R-2 density allows for a higher structure of 5 storeys or 15 meters.

questions.q: What is the Building Height Limit for Residential Maximum R-3?
questions.n: Maximum R-3 zones are high-density and can go up to 12 storeys or 36 meters.

questions.q: What is the Building Height Limit for Residential Cultural Buildings?
questions.n: Cultural buildings are generally allowed a height limit of 30 meters.

questions.q: What are the allowed building projections but excluded on BHL computations?
questions.n: Non-habitable architectural or technical projections like antennas and towers are not counted toward the BHL.

questions.q: What is the maximum building height if RROW is 3 mts.?
questions.n: Narrow roads (3m RROW) strictly limit height to 2 storeys or 6 meters for safety.

questions.q: What is the maximum building height if RROW is 4-5 mts.?
questions.n: A road width of 4-5 meters allows for a height of 2.5 storeys or 7.5 meters.

questions.q: What is the maximum building height if RROW is 6-7 mts.?
questions.n: With a 6-7 meter RROW, the building height is capped at 3 storeys or 9 meters.

questions.q: Which category defines the various building uses in the NBCP?
questions.n: This category groups buildings based on their primary function and the nature of their occupants.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP A -- R1 to R5?
questions.n: Group A covers single-family or low-density residential houses.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP B -- Multiple Dwellings, Convents/Monasteries, Condominiums, Hotels?
questions.n: Group B includes buildings where multiple families or individuals live in separate units.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP C -- Buildings such as Schools, Colleges & Universities?
questions.n: Group C specifically designates educational and recreational facilities.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP D -- Buildings like Mental Hospitals, Asylum, Jails & Prisons, Nursing Home and the likes?
questions.n: Group D covers facilities where people are cared for or confined, categorized as Institutional.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP E -- Buildings such as Gasoline Stations, Office Bldgs, Retails Stores, Malls?
questions.n: Group E is for businesses, offices, and retail trade centers.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP F -- Building such as Factories, Ice Plants, Power Plants, Cold Storage, Cremeries, Workshops?
questions.n: Group F is dedicated to manufacturing and industrial activities.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP G -- Repair Garages, Aircraft Hangars, other workshops using flammable substances?
questions.n: Group G encompasses repair garages and storage facilities for flammable or hazardous materials.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP H -- Assembly other than Group I or 1000 below Occupant Load?
questions.n: Group H is for assembly buildings with a capacity of fewer than 1000 people.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP I -- Assembly above 1000 Occupant Load?
questions.n: Group I is for very large assembly spaces like stadiums or massive theaters.

questions.q: What is the classification for GROUP J -- Buildings such as Agricultural bldgs, private garages, Fence over 1.8mts, tanks, swimming pools?
questions.n: Group J covers minor structures, fences, and auxiliary buildings, known as Accessories.

questions.q: What is the definition of TYPE I Construction?
questions.n: Type I construction is primarily made of wood or other combustible materials.

questions.q: What is the definition of TYPE II Construction?
questions.n: Type II construction is wood-based but with at least a one-hour fire-resistive rating throughout.

questions.q: Which construction type uses Wood and Masonry with Fire-resistive techniques of 1 hour?
questions.n: Type III is the combination of wood and masonry with 1-hour fire resistance.

questions.q: Which construction type uses Concrete Masonry and Steel & Iron with Fire-resistive techniques of 1 hour?
questions.n: Type IV moves to non-combustible materials like steel and iron with 1-hour fire resistance.

questions.q: Which construction type uses Concrete Masonry and Steel & Iron with 4-hour Fire-resistive throughout?
questions.n: Type V is the most fire-resistive construction type, requiring a 4-hour rating throughout.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Dwelling units R1, R2 & R3 with 32-72 sqm?
questions.n: Smaller residential units (32-72 sqm) require one parking slot for every 6 units.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Dwelling units R1, R2 & R3 with 50-96 sqm?
questions.n: Medium-sized units (50-96 sqm) must provide one parking slot for every 4 units.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Dwelling units R1, R2 & R3 with 100-120 sqm?
questions.n: Large residential units (100-120 sqm) require a 1:1 ratio for parking.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Dwelling units R4 with 50-150 sqm?
questions.n: R4 townhouses in this size range require one parking slot per individual unit.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Indigenous Family Dwelling Units?
questions.n: Indigenous family dwellings follow the same ratio as the smallest R1-R3 units.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Condominium Units R5 with 18-22 sqm GFA?
questions.n: Very small R5 condominium units (18-22 sqm) require only one parking slot per 8 units.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Condominium Units R5 with 50 sqm GFA?
questions.n: Medium R5 condo units (50 sqm) require one slot for every 6 units.

questions.q: What is the parking requirement for Condominium Units R5 with 100 sqm GFA?
questions.n: Large condo units (100 sqm) must provide one parking slot for every 4 units.

questions.q: What are the parking space requirements for Hotels?
questions.n: Hotels must provide one car slot per 3 rooms and at least two bus parking slots.

questions.q: What are the parking space requirements for Motels?
questions.n: Motels require a 1:1 ratio as the car is usually parked directly outside the unit.

questions.q: What are the parking space requirements for Bowling Alleys?
questions.n: Bowling alleys must provide one parking slot for every 4 lanes.

questions.q: What are the parking space requirements for Churches and Places of Worships?
questions.n: Churches must provide both car and jeepney slots based on every 50 sqm of floor area.
